selected_lessons.application: The task explicitly prohibits CTA (CTA rule: None). L01 confirms that an informational post about naming conventions as a workflow design constraint should close with a practical observation or next-step note, not a meeting prompt or diagnostic booking request.

steps.instruction: Identify naming conventions as a design constraint specific to one recurring workflow. Use C01 and C02 to define the bounded scope: a small business owner with a repeatable, measurable task where consistent naming (API field labels, form fields, database keys, or human-readable identifiers) affects either AI integration feasibility or manual-to-automated handoff clarity.

Explain why naming convention choices matter before automation. Reference C02 (Bareni workflow spans customer environment, SaaS tools, APIs, and AI prompts) and S01 (owner decision context compares automation investment with manual work or hiring). Show one concrete example: inconsistent customer-ID formats across CRM, invoicing tool, and email records create manual reconciliation friction and block reliable AI extraction or matching.

State the design decision owner faces: standardise naming upfront (before automation) or automate around legacy naming and pay translation cost in prompts, rules, and maintenance. Connect to C04 (human approval mandatory for money movement) if naming affects invoice matching or payment routing.

Define one diagnostic question the owner can use immediately: 'When I move data between my CRM, email, invoicing tool, and spreadsheets this week, how many times do I manually rename or reformat a field to make systems talk to each other?' Ground this in C01 (representative pain: 8–10 hours weekly of repeated work) and S01 (practical, observable decision).

Explain the practical next step without a CTA. Apply L01: close with a neutral action the owner controls. Example: 'Pick one recurring workflow—customer inquiries, invoice processing, or lead tracking—and map how field names flow across your tools this week. Note where you rename or reformat. That map is your naming blueprint.' This preserves S01 (one observable workflow decision) and K03 (human authority remains with owner).

Preserve K01, K03, and K04: use no invented results, no sales urgency, no multi-person team, and no implication that Bareni has solved this for customers. Optionally add a neutral closing: 'Once you have that map, you'll see whether naming standardisation is a one-time fix or an ongoing handoff cost—and whether an automation tool can bridge the gap or whether the cost lives in the naming layer.'

constraints_to_preserve.handling: No customer deployment, invented result, productivity claim, or savings number. Use only the representative scenario (8–10 hours weekly manual work) from C01 as a persona context, not observed proof.
Do not propose autonomous payment or approval. If naming affects invoice automation, reinforce C04: human approval remains mandatory.
Preserve the frozen persona (owner-operator decision context, human authority, no hype), approved evidence status (C01–C05, S01), and founder-to-founder voice. No CTA per task rule.

Use plain English and concrete examples (customer-ID format mismatch, field-name mapping across tools). Keep diagnostic question and next-step action distinct from Bareni capabilities—they are owner-controlled, not Bareni deliverables.
